## Fresh developments (last 24–72 h)

**Signal 1 — DRAM/HBM pricing:** TrendForce Sept 2026: server DRAM contract prices +13–18% QoQ in Q3 2026. Spot HBM3E 36 GB module trading ~$2,100 vs. $300–400 LTA price — extreme spot premium persists. LTAs cap gains for covered customers; non-LTA buyers face steeper hikes.

**Signal 2 — HBM4 ramp:** SK Hynix *slowing* HBM4 ramp (TechPowerUp). Micron targeting 100K HBM wafers/month by year-end; 12-Hi HBM4 at 20–30% of output, targeting 50%. Samsung pacing toward 250K wafers/month. Correction-risk signal remains live: all three suppliers converging on capacity by late 2026 into 2027.

**Signal 3 — Hyperscaler capex:** Big Four 2026 CapEx revised to ~$725B (+77% YoY), above the $600–700B baseline. Amazon raised its 2026 guide to ~$220B explicitly citing higher memory prices. NVIDIA FY2027 consensus now ~$561.5B — 60%+ above the baseline $350B estimate.

**Signal 4 — AMD MI400 / Custom ASIC:** AMD Helios/MI400 (CDNA5, 432 GB HBM4, 40.3 PFLOPS) launched July 2026, now in market. Google TPU v7 Ironwood at 2M+ chips/year. AWS Trainium 3 ramping (1M+ chips). Meta MTIA 400 in testing. Custom-silicon share-shift is live.

**Signal 5 — Optical/photonics:** Coherent (COHR) won a large CPO purchase order from an AI datacenter customer; initial revenue late 2026, larger 2027. Lumentum (LITE) backlog >$400M; secured another multi-hundred-million ultra-high-power laser order (shipments H1 2027); CPO inflection H2 2026 on track. LITE, COHR, IQE on InP allocation since Aug 11; InP fully booked through 2026.

**Signal 6 — Solar:** Trump Section 232 proclamation sets 15% tariff + minimum import prices on polysilicon/cells/modules effective Dec 4, 2026. FSLR endorsed the policy and reaffirmed 2026 guidance ($4.9–5.2B revenue, 17–18.2 GW volume). Cadmium-telluride exemption is a structural moat vs. silicon-dependent rivals.

**Signal 7 — Watchlist catalysts:** See table below.

## Context vs baseline

- Hyperscaler capex at ~$725B now 3–8% above the high end of the $600–700B baseline; memory price inflation is now explicitly cited in Amazon's capex guidance — tight feedback loop confirmed.
- NVIDIA FY2027 consensus ~$561B vs. baseline $350B — thesis materially exceeded.
- AVGO's guide of AI revenue doubling to $115B FY2027 and again to $230B FY2028 is one of the strongest custom-silicon datapoints in the cycle.
- HBM correction risk still live: SK Hynix slowing HBM4 ramp is a first sign of caution as capacity from all three converges into 2027. Not yet a correction signal, but Q4 commentary will be key.

## Most important development

**Broadcom (AVGO) Q3 blowout + Micron (MU) Q4 guide ($50B, 86% GM) together validate that the AI/HBM super-cycle is tracking well ahead of the May 2026 baseline.** AVGO's CEO public guide of AI revenue doubling to ~$115B FY2027 and again to ~$230B FY2028 is a generational forward signal. Micron's $50B quarterly run-rate at 86% gross margins confirms HBM/DRAM pricing power is intact. Near-term read is unambiguously bullish. Key tail risk: 2027 HBM correction as all three suppliers complete capacity expansions; SK Hynix slowing HBM4 ramp is the first real datapoint confirming that risk.
